title: Ordinal Numbers & Fractions
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 37; Ryding Ch. 15)
objectives: Form and agree ordinal numbers 1st–10th (أَوَّلُ / أُولَى, ثَانٍ, ثَالِثٌ ... عَاشِرٌ).
Form classical fractions on the pattern فُعْلٌ (ثُلُثٌ, رُبْعٌ, خُمْسٌ).
Read classical dates and fractional expressions.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 11: What are the four categories of adjectival concordance?

sections.heading: Ordinals Behave as Adjectives
sections.body: Unlike cardinal numbers 3–10 (which show reverse gender), ordinal numbers ('first, second, third...') behave as normal descriptive adjectives: they follow the noun and agree with it in gender, case, and definiteness.

sections.label: Ordinal & Fraction Patterns
sections.summary: Ordinals 2nd–10th follow the active participle pattern فَاعِلٌ (fem. فَاعِلَةٌ), while 'first' is أَوَّلُ (fem. أُولَى). Fractions from 1/3 to 1/10 follow فُعْلٌ (e.g., ثُلُثٌ 'one third', رُبْعٌ 'one quarter'); 'half' is نِصْفٌ.

sections.irab: فِي: حَرْفُ جَرٍّ | اليَوْمِ: اسْمٌ مَجْرُورٌ | الثَّالِثِ: نَعْتٌ مَجْرُورٌ بِالكَسْرَةِ
sections.notes: الثَّالِثِ agrees with اليَوْمِ in gender (masc.), definiteness (الـ), and case (genitive).

sections.heading: Defective Ordinal 'Second' (ثَانٍ)
sections.body: When indefinite nominative or genitive, 'second' drops its yāʾ like قَاضٍ: يَوْمٌ ثَانٍ ('a second day'), but definite is اليَوْمُ الثَّانِي.
